task: Implement a bounded current-main hardening pass for the ED-Finder Codex worker/async bridge based on the missed GitHub review findings from PRs #498, #522 and #525. This is security/process infrastructure only; do not touch product behavior, V3 data/runtime, production systems, credentials, deployment, Stage 27 map code, CRE/CPE mechanics, or Journal work. Read CLAUDE.md and the current control-plane docs first. Address the live issues comprehensively: (1) the final privileged workflow-capable PAT push must not trust Git metadata mutable by the preceding danger-full-access Codex process: do not allow Codex-controlled hooks, remote URLs, credential helpers/includes or equivalent mutable Git state to observe/exfiltrate the token. Prefer a fresh trusted temporary Git metadata/worktree or another demonstrably isolated push path; at minimum canonicalize/validate the GitHub remote from GITHUB_REPOSITORY, disable hooks including pre-push, and fail closed on unexpected Git state. (2) Select CODEX_WORKER_GIT_TOKEN only when .github/workflows/* actually changed; ordinary implementation branches must use GITHUB_TOKEN. (3) Workflow-change detection must fail closed on git/diff errors while treating grep no-match as normal. (4) Remove unnecessary workflow permissions, especially pull-requests: write if not required. (5) Pass potentially long Codex prompts through stdin rather than argv. (6) Prevent unattended workers from inheriting interactive user Codex integrations/config (MCP/hooks/plugins/etc.) where the installed CLI supports an ignore-user-config or equivalent isolated automation mode; preserve authentication but no unrelated external capabilities. (7) Before any Codex process starts, fail closed unless RUNNER_NAME is one of the known dedicated Codex worker hosts documented/proven in repo history (contabo-codex-worker, contabo-codex-worker-2, contabo-codex-worker-3), unless you can prove and safely use an existing dedicated runner label without breaking the pool. Do not invent an unprovisioned label. (8) Update the control-plane docs so they no longer claim the removed serial codex-worker concurrency group and accurately describe the bounded parallel pool. (9) Strengthen test_codex_workers_are_not_globally_serialized so it structurally proves top-level worker concurrency is absent rather than merely banning one literal group name. (10) Add focused regression tests for PAT selection, fail-closed diff detection, trusted push isolation, prompt stdin, user-config isolation and worker identity gating. Preserve the async dispatcher semantics and the three-runner parallel pool. Run focused tests, static checks and git diff --check. If a requested isolation option is unsupported by the installed Codex CLI, do not fake it: implement the strongest repo-controlled isolation available and report the exact residual external-infrastructure requirement. End with changed files, tests/evidence, and residual risks. Do not merge or deploy.
